tour.card.d: Krakie walks you through the tool on the demo project: design, check, transpose, generate. Takes about 5 minutes.
tour.noTarget: This element is not displayed right now.
tour.demo.d: I can create the “automaint” demo project (a garage and its vehicles); you can delete it afterwards.
tour.demo.err: Could not create the demo project.
tour.prop.d: Krakie can show you around the tool in a few minutes.
tour.demo.name: Automaint demo
tour.s.welcome.b: I'm Krakie. We'll follow an ontology's path, from design to files ready to load, on the automaint demo project.
tour.s.nav.b: The menu follows the route: Design, Check, Transpose, Generate. The yellow badge counts the findings waiting for your decision.
tour.s.target.b: Curiosity or Neo4j: the analysis, the model and the exports adapt to this choice. Switch at any time to compare.
tour.s.dashboard.b: It shows where the project stands and suggests the next action. Each card opens the matching stage.
tour.s.ed-canvas.b: Classes and their relationships are drawn as a diagram. Click a class: the inspector on the right shows its details and lets you edit them.
tour.s.ed-quick.b: One line of text is one axiom, for example “ElectricVehicle < Vehicle”. The graph updates instantly, with no clicking around.
tour.s.list.b: The class tree is on the left and the sheet of the selected class on the right: parents, properties, restrictions. Handy for browsing a large ontology.
tour.s.shapes.b: They describe what the data should look like: required fields, cardinalities, allowed values. Generate them from the ontology, then fine-tune them.
tour.s.conformite.b: OntoForge checks the OWL 2 and RDFS profiles and cites the specification for every point to fix. It is better to settle these before transposing.
tour.s.shacl.b: Drop in an RDF file: each violation is tied to its shape, and Krakie can explain it. This lets you test your rules on real data.
tour.s.an-counters.b: What moves to a property graph on its own, what needs your decision, and what might be lost. Ambiguous cases are never settled without you.
tour.s.an-finding.b: Each finding lists its options with their impact and flags the one I recommend for your target. Pick one, or apply the recommendation to a whole rule at once.
tour.s.model.b: This is the resulting property graph: node types, relationships and validations. Click a node to see its properties, its keys and where it comes from in the ontology.
tour.s.exports.b: These are the files ready to load into the chosen target. Copy a file, or download the full zip.
tour.s.q-nl.b: Write it in plain language: it is turned into a guided sentence, with a confidence score. Words that were not recognized can be linked to a class or a relationship.
tour.s.q-values.b: The query is built like a sentence, so no SPARQL is needed. “is one of…” offers the known values, completed from the endpoint.
tour.s.q-endpoint.b: To query a SPARQL endpoint without saving it: URL, authentication, graph. The secret is kept in memory for this session only.
tour.s.fab.b: This button, or Ctrl+K, opens the assistant: it knows which screen and selection you are on. That is the end of the tour; you can restart it from the top bar.
